Normalize the counts

Source: R/normalize_data.R
normalize_data.Rd

Normalizes the counts to counts per million (CPM), so that samples sequenced at different depths can be compared. Run it before compute_data_table. Three methods are available:

  • "cpm" (default): each count is divided by the total number of reads of its sample and multiplied by 1e6.

  • "tmm": as "cpm", but the library sizes are corrected with the trimmed mean of M-values (TMM) normalization factors of edgeR (normLibSizes). This is more robust when strong hits deplete a large part of the library.

  • "control": each count is divided by the number of reads of the control barcodes (for example non-targeting shRNAs) of its sample and multiplied by 1e6. This assumes that the control barcodes are not affected by the treatment.

The normalization only affects the normalized count table (and so the data table, the Z-score and the plots). The edgeR based methods (CAMERA, ROAST) always model the raw counts.

Usage

normalize_data(
  screenR_Object,
  method = c("cpm", "tmm", "control"),
  control_barcodes = NULL
)

Arguments

screenR_Object

The ScreenR object obtained using create_screenr_object.

method

The normalization method: "cpm" (default), "tmm" or "control".

control_barcodes

The barcodes to use for the "control" method (required by that method, ignored by the others).

Value

The ScreenR object with the normalized count table (see get_normalized_count_table).

See also

compute_data_table, get_normalized_count_table, remove_all_zero_row

Examples

object <- get0("object", envir = asNamespace("ScreenR"))
object <- normalize_data(object)

get_normalized_count_table(object)
